findings.evidence: dev-platform/checks.toml (diff lines 55-58) sets patterns = [AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/**, openspec/specs/**, dev-platform/capabilities/**]. It omits explorer/nodes/**, explorer/map.toml, explorer/editorial-review.json, explorer/assets/** and scripts/build_explorer.py. A malformed node, such as an unfinished sentence, is therefore not caught by selected checks. It is caught only by the test group or the Explorer workflow.
findings.summary: The new `explorer` check fires only on edits to bound source files. It does not fire on edits to the Explorer's own inputs.

findings.evidence: scripts/select_checks.py main() (diff lines 4593-4603) sets `code = exit_request.code`. That value may be None or a string. If `run_template` ends the process another way, such as `os.exec*` or a process-level exit, the drift step is skipped without notice. The wrapper also runs `build_explorer.py drift --base`, which builds the full site and aborts on any editorial error. A selected-checks run unrelated to the Explorer can therefore fail on an editorial or tooling problem, which contradicts the 'tool error only' docstring.
findings.summary: The `select_checks.py` wrapper catches `SystemExit` from `run_template`, and its exit-code handling is fragile. It also builds the whole site for every `--execute` run.

findings.evidence: scripts/build_explorer.py mark_reviewed (diff lines 4360-4376) copies `site.digests` verbatim into the review record. The review is a single committed JSON blob with no reviewer or commit metadata. A one-line `--all` run silences all drift, so the advisory signal is easy to defeat. The note in the drift-issue body encourages running it per node, but nothing enforces that.
findings.summary: `mark-reviewed --all` stamps whatever the sources currently contain, and it prunes obsolete records. Nothing links the stamp to an actual review.
